header:
Mortgage interest
in the early years

lines.text: Your first mortgage payment can be 88% interest.
lines.say: Your first mortgage payment can be eighty-eight percent interest.

lines.text: In late September 2026, the average 30-year rate topped 7% (7.03%, Freddie Mac).
lines.say: In late September twenty twenty-six, the average thirty-year rate topped seven percent, hitting seven point oh three.

lines.text: Borrow $400,000 over 30 years at that rate, and the payment's $2,669 a month.
lines.say: Borrow four hundred thousand over thirty years at that rate, and the payment's twenty-six sixty-nine dollars a month.

lines.text: Why? Interest is charged on what you still owe. $400,000 x 7.03% / 12 = about $2,343.
lines.say: Why? Interest is charged on what you still owe. Four hundred thousand times seven point oh three percent, divided by twelve, is about two thousand three hundred forty-three dollars.

lines.text: Only about $326 pays down the loan.
lines.say: Only about three hundred twenty-six dollars pays down the loan.

lines.text: After a year, you've paid $32,031, but the balance dropped just $4,040.
lines.say: After a year, you've paid about thirty-two thousand, but the balance dropped just four thousand and forty.

lines.text: Interest shrinks with the balance, but principal doesn't win until year 21.
lines.say: Interest shrinks with the balance, but principal doesn't win until year twenty-one.

lines.text: Which means any extra principal paid early cuts the balance that all future interest is charged on.
lines.say: Which means any extra principal paid early cuts the balance that all future interest is charged on.

lines.text: In this example, an extra $100 a month saves about $73,000 in interest.
lines.say: In this example, an extra hundred a month saves about seventy-three thousand in interest.

scene.label: Extra $100/month, same loan
scene.sub: interest saved; paid off 39 months sooner

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Why your first mortgage payment is 88% interest
post.ig:
Your first mortgage payment can be 88% interest.
On a $400,000, 30-year loan at 7.03% (Freddie Mac's 30-year average in late September 2026), the payment is $2,669.
Month one: $2,343 is interest and only $326 pays down the loan.
After a year of payments ($32,031), the balance drops just $4,040. Principal doesn't overtake interest until year 21.
Sources: Freddie Mac PMMS (Sept 24, 2026); example math is standard amortization.
News and education, not financial advice.
